analysis:
Only the BASE text of .github/workflows/provider-tests.yml and a truncated patch excerpt were supplied. No HEAD text was provided for this file. The visible patch adds a build-cluster job that builds once on a large runner and hands debug test products to test jobs via .github/actions/provider-ci-products. It also moves the path-dependent workspace link, reworks provider and cluster test job steps, and changes runner routing and plan handling. These are CI changes with no production code path, and the artifact handoff is not in the supplied excerpt.

Base side: the workflow keeps contents:read permissions, uses SHA-pinned actions, sets persist-credentials:false, and saves caches only on pushes to master or dev (SAVE_CACHES at line 37). PR runs restore but never save caches, which limits cache poisoning from PRs. The base text contains no secrets, no release-signing steps and no publication steps. Nothing in the visible lines touches the provider runtime, the attestation/App Attest boundaries (TB-009, TB-011), or the prefix cache (T-041, TB-007). The prefix-cache environment variables at lines 253-254 and 263-264 only set DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0 for test gates, which is test-only and does not change production defaults.

Unverified items for integration: (1) whether the new product handoff (artifact or cache) between build and test jobs verifies integrity and is scoped per run, so a PR cannot poison products consumed by master or dev test jobs; (2) whether the new job-level permissions stay minimal; (3) whether strict_cache and the release-bound builds on master are unaffected by the shared products. The HEAD text and the provider-ci-products action were not supplied, so these cannot be confirmed or refuted. No concrete regression is supported by the visible evidence.
